newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end off, feeders mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end off, feeders mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed lower, knocked down by commercial selling while feeder cattle futures ended mixed with deferreds again setting contract highs on concern that cold weather will cut feeder numbers, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.350 to 0.100 cent per lb lower with February off 0.125 at 65.850 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.325 cent lower to 0.300 higher with March off most at 68.175 cents. Lightly traded distant August through November feeder contracts posted new contract highs for the second day.
Persistent cold weather played a part in both contracts, traders said.

Commercial selling in live cattle reflected concern the bitter cold weather forecast to move through main population centers will cut beef demand. This generally offset the current strength in cash cattle prices, they said.
"The cold is moving into beef consumption areas and out of beef growing areas," said Jim Clarkson from A and A Inc.

Adding to weakness in back months of live cattle were expectations of increased fed cattle marketings going into the spring. Placements into feedlot were large late in 1996, which should be confirmed by next week's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report.

R.J. O'Brien sold much of the day with RBH, Lind-Waldock, ADM Investor Services and Rosenthal Collins early sellers in February. Cargill Investor Services bought late. Lind-Waldock and Prudential Securities sold April early while E.D.&F. Man and Dean Witter bought, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, commission houses bought February 66 calls and commercials sold 68 calls early. Commercials continued to do risk reversals in April and June, buying puts and selling calls, pit sources added.
Nearby feeder cattle were dragged down by weakness in live cattle but deferreds posted new highs on long-term ideas.

Back months were strong on the outlook for reduced feeder supplies by next fall, especially with the current cold weather pattern likely to affect the calf crop. The cold and poor feeding conditions will weaken cows and in turn, calves that are born into the spring, traders said.
"The spring calf crop is going to be in trouble," said Julia Bussie, livestock analyst with A G Edwards.
E.D.& F. Man bought August late after early buying by Smith Barney in deferreds. LFG also bought back months early while R.J. O'Brien bought March, pit sources said.
The CME feeder cattle index rose $0.15 to $68.48 per cwt. The price was the highest since March 20, 1995.
